name: Microsoft Hyper-V
author: Netlens
description: Shows your Hyper-V hosts with their virtual machines: state, processors, memory, start time, network switch, and each VM matched to the device Netlens found by its MAC address (then IP), so a VM is one device linked to its host. Reads through Windows Remote Management (WinRM over HTTPS) by running one fixed, read-only Get-VM script. Needs a user on the Hyper-V machine that may use remote management and Hyper-V; the settings page has the PowerShell lines to set that up.

info.title: What to run on the Hyper-V machine (PowerShell as administrator)
info.text: Run this once on the Hyper-V host, in a PowerShell window opened as administrator. It makes a user for Netlens that can use remote management and Hyper-V (and nothing else), switches on WinRM over HTTPS with a self-signed certificate and opens port 5986 only to the machine Netlens runs on. Change the first line to the address of that machine. Then enter https://<this host's address>:5986, the user name (netlens) and its password below, and keep 'Verify TLS certificate' off while the certificate is self-signed. The 'Hyper-V Administrators' group can also manage the virtual machines, so use a long password, and keep the firewall rule.
info.code:
$netlens = '192.168.0.189'   # the address of the machine Netlens runs on
$pw = Read-Host -AsSecureString 'Password for the netlens user'
New-LocalUser -Name netlens -Password $pw -PasswordNeverExpires -UserMayNotChangePassword -Description 'Netlens (read Hyper-V)'
Add-LocalGroupMember -Group 'Hyper-V Administrators' -Member netlens
Add-LocalGroupMember -Group 'Remote Management Users' -Member netlens
Enable-PSRemoting -Force -SkipNetworkProfileCheck
$cert = New-SelfSignedCertificate -DnsName $env:COMPUTERNAME -CertStoreLocation Cert:\LocalMachine\My -NotAfter (Get-Date).AddYears(10)
New-Item -Path WSMan:\localhost\Listener -Transport HTTPS -Address * -CertificateThumbPrint $cert.Thumbprint -Force
Get-ChildItem WSMan:\localhost\Listener | Where-Object Keys -contains 'Transport=HTTP' | Remove-Item -Recurse -Force
Get-NetFirewallRule -Name 'WINRM-HTTP-In-TCP*' | Disable-NetFirewallRule
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName 'Netlens WinRM HTTPS' -Direction Inbound -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 5986 -RemoteAddress $netlens -Action Allow

config.label: Hyper-V hosts
config.help: One line per Hyper-V host: its address (https://host:5986, port 5986 is the default), and the user name and password of the Netlens user on that Windows machine (a local user is just the name, a domain user is DOMAIN\name). Fill in the host's own address under More when the first field is a name, so Netlens can find its device.

columns.label: Host's own address
columns.help: Only needed when the address above is a name

options.label: NTLM (default, works with local and domain users)
Basic (only when you turned Basic on in WinRM)

config.label: Verify TLS certificate
config.help: Leave this off while the host uses a self-signed certificate (what the setup lines create).
